summary: 1936 CCC-built two-story lookout in Madison County, NC; repainted 2009 with an FFLA grant; 2024 water-damage repairs postponed. Staffing reportedly stopped circa 2000.

facts.design: two-story lookout with wooden cab and catwalk on a rock foundation
facts.status_note: Standing, but needs water-damage repairs; the 2024 repair grant was returned in 2025 when the work was postponed.
facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

events.note: Built by the CCC for the US Forest Service
Transferred to the NC Forest Service
Registered March 1, 1998 as US 256, NC 6; nominated by R. Fred Foster, North Carolina Registrar
Staffing stopped circa 2000, per the 2024 FFLA report; the 1998 Register entry still says it was staffed
NC Forest Service replaced the tower roof
Wes Greene repainted the entire tower over several weekends, using the first FFLA emergency stabilization grant ($150)
Rededication at the tower mentioned in the 2009 NC chapter report
FFLA $500 restoration grant to Bo Dossett for water-damage repairs; work not yet begun
The 2024 restoration grant was returned because the work was postponed, with other funding expected when the project resumes

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1998 Register entry says the NC Forest Service continues to staff the tower; the 2024 FFLA report says staffing stopped circa 2000 and the tower is no longer in use. Both may have been accurate when written; the story gives the newer report more weight.

The Register names the North Carolina Division of Forest Resources; the 2024 and 2025 FFLA reports say North Carolina Forest Service (NCFS). The story uses the Register's name and notes the NCFS in the sources.

notes_for_editor: Access and rental status are not confirmed by any source read, so no access key is set. Staffing conflicts between the 1998 Register and the 2024 FFLA report; the story gives both. The brief's 2008 roof, 2009 grant ($150) and steward details, and the 2024/2025 grant events are verified against the FFLA reports. The brief's tnlandforms.us source only lists the tower with a survey code and was not used. The 1936 CCC build and 1966 transfer come from the NHLR page alone. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the planned-repairs sentence no longer attributes the water-damage purpose to the flashing, and the 2025 return now gives both reasons the report states.
